set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Box puzzle
set.stimulus:
Eight boxes — P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W — are kept one above another in a single stack, but not necessarily in the same order. The bottommost position is numbered 1 and the topmost position is numbered 8. Each box contains a different item — Bottles, Bags, Candles, Caps, Clocks, Watches, Lamps and Shoes.

1. Less than three boxes are kept between box P and the box containing Watches.
2. As many boxes are kept below box R as above box W.
3. Only one box is kept between the box containing Shoes and the box containing Bags.
4. Box R contains Bottles.
5. More than five boxes are kept below the box containing Clocks.
6. Only two boxes are kept between box U and the box containing Candles, and box U is kept above the box containing Candles.
7. More than two boxes are kept below the box containing Shoes.
8. Box W is kept below box T.
9. As many boxes are kept below the box containing Bags as above box S.
10. Neither box V nor box Q is kept at an odd-numbered position.
11. Only three boxes are kept between box R and box V, and box R is kept above box V.
12. Only one box is kept between box Q and box V, and box Q is kept above box V.
13. The box containing Lamps is kept at an even-numbered position.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which box is kept at the top?

steps: No clue fixes a position outright, so begin with the clues that limit the options most.
Now the box containing Clocks can be at position 7 or position 8 (clue 5) — make 2 cases.
Case the box containing Clocks at position 8: every sub-case breaks clues 4, 11 and 12 — rejected.
Case the box containing Clocks at position 7 survives.
Now box Q can be at position 2, position 4, position 6 or position 8 (clue 10) — make 4 cases.
Case box Q at position 2: clue 12 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box Q at position 6: every sub-case breaks clue 9 — rejected.
Case box Q at position 8: clue 11 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box Q at position 4 survives.
Clues 10 and 12 → box V at position 2; Clue 11 → box R at position 6.
Clue 2 → box W at position 3; Clue 4 → the box containing Bottles at position 6.
Now the box containing Shoes can be at position 4, position 5 or position 8 (clue 7) — make 3 cases.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 5: clue 9 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 8: clue 3 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 4 survives.
Clue 3 → the box containing Bags at position 2; Clue 9 → box S at position 7.
The box containing Lamps takes the only place left: position 8.
Now box P can be at position 1, position 5 or position 8 — make 3 cases.
Case box P at position 5: clue 6 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box P at position 8: clue 6 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box P at position 1 survives.
Continuing the same way, the remaining clues fix everyone.
Final arrangement (top to bottom): U, S, R, T, Q, W, V, P.
From the final arrangement, position 8 → **U**.
solution.shortcut: No clue fixes a position outright: start with the clue that leaves the fewest cases, write each case down and let the remaining clues kill the wrong ones.
solution.trap: **S** would be at position 8 only if clue 3 were ignored — clue 3 rules that arrangement out.
